blocks.text: If we believe the Jews, the gods of the Sepharvites, Adrammelech and Anammelech, mentioned in 2 Reg. XVII, 31., were worshipped in the form of peacocks and pheasants, or of quails. Kimchi on that passage: ובירושלמי אדרמלך וענמלך זה טווס ופסיוני וטווס הוא הנקרא בלשון לע״ז פאון וידוע הוא ופסיוני הוא שלו והרגים שאלו ויבא שלו שאלו בסרא ואייתי פסיונין, In the Jerusalem Talmud (in the tractate On Idolatry), Adrammelech and Anammelech, that is, ταὼς [taōs] and pheasant. And ταὼς [taōs] is the same as peacock, the name of an idol, which is well known. And the pheasant, that is, the quail. For at Ps. CV, 40., for the words „They asked, and he brought quails,“ „the Targum has, They asked for meat, and he brought pheasants“. But in the Babylonian Talmud, tractate Sanhedrin ch. 7, fol. 63 b, Adrammelech and Anammelech are rendered הפרד והסוס, the mule and the horse. Both are false, or uncertain. For it is customary with these men to blurt out whatever comes into their mouths, and to smear their dreams onto paper.
